chamada: For the day on the street: the screen gets simpler, numbers disappear, photos with people ask for a check before going out, and panic, “I’m safe” and the no-signal guide stay at hand.

itens: No like, reply or follower numbers on screen
Before posting a photo: a reminder to check and blur faces
Licence plate, CPF, phone number or address in the text: a warning before it goes out
Photos go out without the hidden file data: place, device and time
chave.soAqui: It stays on this device only, and nobody finds out you turned it on.

estouBem.texto: One tap tells your safety contacts that you are safe. It goes only to people you chose and who accepted, carries no location and disappears in 24 hours.
estouBem.feito: Done: {n} contacts received it. The message disappears in 24 hours.
estouBem.feitoUm: Done: 1 contact received it. The message disappears in 24 hours.
estouBem.semContatos: To send it, choose a safety contact below and wait for them to accept.

contatos.texto: Up to 10 people you trust. Each one accepts before receiving any message from you, and only you see this list.
contatos.pedido: Request sent. The person answers in their own Protest mode.
contatos.pedidosTitulo: Asked you to be their contact
contatos.limite: You already have 10 contacts. Remove one to ask someone else.
contatos.naoEncontrado: We couldn’t find that @, or it is not possible to ask that account.

recados.viaOrg: It came through the legal support of {org}.
passos: Call the organisation’s legal support line or the city’s Public Defender’s Office.
Find out which police station the person was taken to. Bring an ID of theirs if you have one.
Tell their family or the person they usually name.
Do not spread their name in public unless they or their family agree.

detido.texto: Sends a ready-made message to your safety contacts and, if you choose, to an organisation’s legal support. No location and no free text: nobody reads anything beyond “I was detained”.
detido.feitoOrg: The legal support received it too.
detido.panico: If you need to, also use the panic button above: it signs your account out of every device.
direitos: Give your name and show an ID. About everything else, you have the right to remain silent.
Ask to speak to a lawyer or to the Public Defender’s Office.
Ask them to tell your family or the person you name.
Ask for the name of whoever arrested you and which police station you are going to.
Do not sign anything without reading it, and preferably not without your lawyer present.
Within 24 hours you must be brought before a judge, at the custody hearing. Say there if there was violence.
detido.semContatos: To send it, choose a safety contact (and wait for them to accept) or a legal support.

assessoria.texto: Whoever manages a verified organisation publishes its legal support line here: who answers and how to call. Anyone detained who chooses the organisation alerts whoever manages its account.
assessoria.ajuda: 10 to 400 characters. Leave it empty to remove.

semSinal.texto: The guide for when the internet goes down. Open it once now: afterwards it opens on this device even without internet.

verificar.cpf: The text has a CPF ({trecho}). Remove it before posting.
verificar.telefone: The text has a phone number ({trecho}). Remove it before posting.
verificar.email: The text has an email address ({trecho}). Remove it before posting.
verificar.endereco: The text has a street address with a number ({trecho}). Remove it before posting.
verificar.placa: The text seems to have a licence plate ({trecho}). A plate leads to a person. Tap post again to send it anyway.
verificar.fixo: The text seems to have a phone number ({trecho}). Tap post again to send it anyway.
verificar.foto: Protest mode: check whether anyone’s face shows and blur it before posting. Tap post again to send it anyway.

erros.falha: That didn’t work right now. Try again.
erros.semServico: Alumia has no connection to the database right now.
erros.desligado: This part has been turned off by the coordination.
erros.muitos: Too many attempts in a row. Wait a minute.

guia.chamada: What to do when the internet goes down in the middle of a protest. This guide stays saved on this device after the first visit.

itens: Open this guide once with internet: from then on it opens without a network.
Agree with your group on a meeting point and a time, in case you get separated.
Write down on paper two trusted phone numbers and the legal support number.
Leave with a full battery and, if you can, a power bank.
Calls and SMS sometimes get through even when the internet doesn’t. Short messages work better.
With lots of people together the network gets congested: a higher or more open spot helps.
When you can, send one short message at a time instead of many attempts in a row.
Without signal, the phone uses a lot of battery searching for a network. Airplane mode stops that search.
With airplane mode on, the phone does not talk to the carrier’s antennas: it gets no calls and does not register with them either.
You can turn Wi-Fi or Bluetooth on while airplane mode is on.
Turn airplane mode off only to call or send a message, and turn it on again afterwards.
There are apps that pass messages from one phone to another over Bluetooth, without internet (mesh networks).
They are not part of Alumia. If your group is going to use one, install and test it together before the protest.
Say you are safe through Protest mode: it goes only to your safety contacts.
If someone from the group did not show up at the meeting point, contact the legal support line.
